Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law · Money, work & business

document noun

an official paper

also documents, papers, paperwork, official document

classical

Quint. 12.8.12: omne lītis īnstrūmentum
Suet. Calig. 8: pūblicī īnstrūmentī auctōritās (Lewis & Short)

īnstrūmentum, īnstrūmentī n.

noun, second declension

a document, a deed; in the plural, the papers of a case or a business

Of writings, an instrument, document or record (Lewis & Short): post-Augustan prose and the jurists. Otherwise īnstrūmentum is a tool or equipment, so the context must show the sense.

Examples

  • ideōque opus est intuērī omne lītis īnstrūmentum; quod vidēre nōn est satis, perlegendum erit.

    So you must look over all the documents of the case: seeing them is not enough, they must be read through.Quint. 12.8.12

Other words

  • tabulae, tabulārum f. pl. — written records: accounts, registers, a will

    noun, first declension, plural · also used · classical · Cic. Arch. 8: tabulae pūblicae, the public records (Lewis & Short)

    Cicero’s word for documents kept on record, from the writing-tablets they were written on.

  • diplōma, diplōmatis n. — an official document granting a privilege

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · M-O s.v. document: official document; Cic. Fam. 6.12.3 (Lewis & Short)

    A letter folded double: a state warrant or passport for travel, later any document by which a magistrate granted a favour (Lewis & Short).

  • documentum, documentī n. — a lesson, an example, a warning; a proof

    noun, second declension · avoid · classical · Traupman 106, 366: documentō est, this proves

    A false friend for a paper document: classically what teaches, a lesson or a warning (Lewis & Short). Traupman keeps it for a file on a computer (see document, on a computer).

See also document, sign, paper.
